I have been working this land for sixty years and I know every corner of my 11.6 mu. My wife and I are getting older — two people cannot manage too many complicated things. I keep the same four crops I have grown for years because I know how they behave. Cotton is my money crop, maize feeds the family and the animals, peanuts I sell and eat, mungbeans I plant partly to rest the soil in one small patch and partly to sell at the village market.

For my spring maize, I put in the most land — about 4.6 mu — because it is reliable. I always buy hybrid seeds from the township seed shop. I put down base fertilizer before planting — a bag of compound fertilizer mixed with some urea — then top-dress around jointing time. My well lets me irrigate four times: before sowing, at seedling, at jointing, and when the ears fill. I use rotary tillage with the rented machine each spring.

Cotton I give 3.5 mu. I always buy Bt hybrid cotton seeds now, been doing that for over fifteen years — fewer worms to spray for, though I still spray for aphids and whitefly many times. Cotton needs the most watching and the most water. I irrigate five times and spray maybe seven times through the season. It earns the most money so I protect it carefully.

Peanuts get 2 mu. I use improved local variety seeds from the county market. Peanuts like deep soil so I plough this plot rather than rotary-till. I apply less nitrogen — peanuts fix their own — but I still put phosphorus and potassium. I irrigate three times.

Mungbeans take the last 1.5 mu, a smaller sandy patch. I keep seed from last year's harvest — I have been doing this my whole life with mungbeans. They need the least inputs. Two irrigations, two sprays, rotary tillage.
